display_name: Mercury ruler of the 1st House in the 1st House
description: You eat with the analyst-mind: portions, ingredients, timing, cleanliness all matter to you instinctively. The body is Vata-Pitta dominant — wiry frame, sharp digestion when calm, susceptible to anxiety-driven indigestion. Best diet: warm, cooked, predictable, eaten in a quiet environment on a tight schedule. Avoid raw, cold, irregular eating. Cumin, ginger, fennel, ajwain settle the nervous-stomach. Skip kale-and-cold-salad culture; choose khichdi, soups, stewed vegetables. The shadow: over-analyzing the meal into a research project — at some point food is just nourishment, not data.

display_name: Mercury ruler of the 10th House in the 1st House
description: Career-anxiety lands in the stomach first. The deadline week, the pitch day, the audit weekend all show up as digestive turbulence before they show up in the calendar. Pre-meeting meals must be light, warm, cooked — never heavy or raw. Ginger tea before high-stakes presentations. The shadow: skipping meals in deadline mode — the body pays interest on the missed meal for three days.

display_name: Moon ruler of the 11th House in the 11th House
description: Friend-circle dinners, community feasts, women-led-network potlucks are deep-nourishment occasions. Moon-Cancer in 11H loves warm, milky, gentle foods — kheer, kichari, soft rice, sweet curd. Mass-audience comfort food (the kind grandma cooked for 30 cousins) feels like home. The shadow: emotional eating in public — the friend-circle table is a place where the food and the warmth blur.

display_name: Sun ruler of the 12th House in the 12th House
description: Retreat-style eating practice. Solo meals, monastery-style meals, ashram food all carry extra nourishment for you. Sun-in-Leo-12H favors warm, sattvic, simple food eaten in silence or near-silence. Pitru tarpan and ancestral-offering rituals before meals are quietly powerful. The shadow: the kingly appetite that wants too much when alone — portion the plate, then sit.

display_name: Jupiter ruler of the 4th House in the 4th House
description: Hamsa Yoga on the home-throne. The home kitchen is the medicine. Mother's recipes, family-business food, slow-cooked grandmother dishes are deeply nourishing. Sagittarian-Jupiter favors warming, sattvic, traditional cuisine — ghee, dal, rice, kichari, slow-cooked meats with whole-spice. Cooking *at home* is itself a healing ritual. Avoid restaurant-heavy weeks. The shadow: comfort-food expansion can quietly settle into Kapha layers — Jupiter in 4th expands the body too.

display_name: Jupiter ruler of the 7th House in the 4th House

The shadow: dependency on the partner for nourishment that the body should also know to produce alone.

display_name: Saturn ruler of the 5th House in the 5th House
description: Saturn-on-creative-throne brings discipline to the eating schedule. Best practice: same time, same plate, same quantity — the body responds to ritual. Sweet-warm grains (rice, wheat-roti, oats) ground the Vata mind into the body. The 5H also rules child-feeding — you instinctively know what to feed children but may forget yourself. Cold, dry, raw food (Saturn-Vata-tilt) destabilizes; choose warm, oily, cooked. The shadow: rigidity that becomes a punishment — eating discipline should bring peace, not tension.

display_name: Saturn ruler of the 6th House in the 5th House

display_name: Venus ruler of the 2nd House in the 7th House

Pisces-Venus tilt favors refined, watery, sweet foods (fish, rice puddings, white-cheese-and-honey, soft fruits). The shadow: sugar-and-comfort tilt at the partner-table; the love-eats-too-much pattern. Pair sweetness with bitter greens to keep the liver happy.

display_name: Venus ruler of the 9th House in the 7th House

display_name: Mars ruler of the 3rd House in the 8th House

The shadow: skipping meals in the heat of communication-fire — set a meal alarm.
